name: Austromarxism
summary: Austromarxism was the Vienna school of Marxist socialism of about 1900 to 1934, led by Otto Bauer, Max Adler, Rudolf Hilferding and Karl Renner. It combined a Marxist analysis of class struggle and finance capital with a commitment to winning power by universal suffrage in a democratic republic, socialising large property while leaving small working property, and settling national conflicts by national cultural autonomy. It stood between reformist social democracy and Bolshevism.
scope: The profile represents the party-programme Austromarxism of Otto Bauer: the 1926 Linz Programme of the Austrian Social Democratic Workers' Party (the key statement, drafted by Bauer), his 1907 work on the national question with the 1899 Brunn nationality programme, and his articles of 1908 to 1911 and 1936. It does not cover Renner's later politics, Adler's epistemology, the party's wartime or 1938 positions, or the practice of Red Vienna, and it uses no source on single-theorist views other than Bauer's. Austrian party practice and Austromarxist theory are not identical (source s3).

universal-healthcare.rationale: Section IV demands compulsory health, accident, old-age and survivors insurance for all employees, small traders, small farmers and professionals, with federal subsidies and municipal medicine supply; this is near-universal state-backed coverage rather than a tax-funded service.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Section I blames the planlessness of capitalist production for price swings, overwork, crises and unemployment, and section V offers planned expansion of social production in its place, so an adherent rejects the claim.

public-ownership.rationale: Section V requires transfer of large estates, mining, large industry and transport to the ownership of the community (state, province or municipality) or to public bodies and cooperatives.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Section IV demands expanded progressive income, wealth, inheritance and luxury taxes and higher taxation of property income than of earned income.

unions-good.rationale: The programme defends the right of association of workers, employees and officials, puts the party's political power at the service of trade-union struggles and credits unions with winning better conditions.

property-fundamental.rationale: Section V provides for expropriating large landowners and capitalists, with compensation depending on the circumstances at the time, which treats private property as overridable.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Section IV demands tighter state supervision of banks, cartels and industrial concerns, a cartel law, and state control of the central bank credit and interest policy.

cut-welfare.rationale: The whole social-policy section demands expanding unemployment, health, old-age and family insurance and social care; cutting welfare is the opposite of the programme.

worker-ownership.rationale: Socialised firms are to be run as state, provincial or municipal firms, public institutions or cooperatives, so ownership by the workers of each firm is one permitted form among several and the programme warns against narrow sectional worker interests.

central-planning.rationale: Section V says socialism needs areas large enough for socialist planned economy and replaces capital accumulation by planned enlargement of the social apparatus of production; the programme does not say how centralised the plan is.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The programme lists expansion of progressive inheritance taxes and uses wealth and inheritance taxes to pay off compensation bonds for expropriated owners.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Section IV demands the international dismantling of protective tariff systems to let the division of labour between peoples develop.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The programme asks for state promotion of the settlement and growth of new industries, use of natural energy sources and transport, and concentration of public works in slumps.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Section V keeps small working property of artisans and peasants but places large holdings with the community, so property concentrated in the state is the programme's answer, not wide private spread.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The programme wants a stable currency and stricter state supervision of the central bank, which presupposes keeping it.

one-party-rule.rationale: The programme pledges to exercise power in democratic forms with press, association and assembly freedom, and Bauer in 1936 defends freedom to form parties against fascist one-party rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Section III celebrates the party having overthrown the monarchy and founded the democratic republic, and describes the monarchy as rule of dynasty, generals and bureaucracy.

democracy-best.rationale: The programme commits to conquering and exercising state power by universal suffrage and under democratic guarantees, while allowing dictatorship against a bourgeois counter-revolution.

workers-councils.rationale: Section III aims at winning the majority by universal suffrage in the democratic republic; works councils appear only as bodies of co-determination in workplaces.

political-violence-never.rationale: Section III accepts civil war if the bourgeoisie destroys democracy and dictatorship against sabotage and armed revolt, so violence is justified in defined cases.

war-builds-character.rationale: Section I fears wars that threaten to destroy all civilisation and section VI fights imperialist and nationalist wars, so war is not valued.

separate-church-state.rationale: Section IV.7 demands separation of state and church, churches as private-law bodies, and no public funds for religious purposes.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Section IV.7 makes all worldviews equal before the law and demands civil marriage and secular schools, which excludes law founded on scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Section IV demands elected judges, jurors and lay assessors, democratic supervision of police and prisons, and a republican army and police, all public.

military-superiority.rationale: Section VI demands planned international disarmament and peaceful relations with all states, opposing an arms race.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Bauer defines the nation as a community of character produced by shared fate and culture, not descent, and the programme condemns oppression of national minorities.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The programme says the history of the democratic republic is the history of class struggle, and Bauer applies the Marxist class analysis to the history of the nations.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Section V says the development of productive forces becomes the means to raise living standards, health and culture once socialised; only capitalist war threatens civilisation.

revolution-justified.rationale: Section III states that if bourgeois counter-revolution destroys democracy, the working class could win state power only through civil war.

gradual-change.rationale: The programme says social democracy must burst the barriers of capitalist society, and Bauer warns against reformism that forgets the aim of overturning the whole building.

direct-action.rationale: Power is to be won by majority and universal suffrage, and Bauer treats anti-parliamentary syndicalism as a product of failed cross-class blocs.

production-for-use.rationale: Section II.4 contrasts a society that sacrifices public health and happiness to profit-seeking with one that makes the economy serve health and human happiness.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The programme speaks of classes that profit from the exploitation of others' labour and of the exploitative property of capitalists to be abolished.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Dictatorship is allowed only against sabotage, armed revolt or foreign-backed counter-revolution while democratic guarantees are the normal rule; the party distanced itself from Bolshevism.

collective-farming.rationale: Section V keeps peasants' working property and promotes only gradual voluntary cooperatives.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Section I.6 says competition for colonial territories creates ever new clashes between the capitalist world powers and permanent war danger.

taxation-theft.rationale: The programme builds its finance on expanding progressive taxes and uses them for social policy.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Bauer's national programme makes nations public-law corporations holding autonomous powers, so rights attach to national groups as well as individuals.

organic-representation.rationale: The programme rests on party competition under universal suffrage and Bauer praises the end of estate-based privilege.

total-state.rationale: The programme promises press, association and assembly freedom and Bauer in 1936 defends personal liberty against fascist state control.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Section VI resists imperialist and nationalist wars and seeks the Anschluss only by peaceful means.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The programme rests authority on elected representation and condemns dynastic rule; Bauer praises binding power to laws.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Sections IV and V demand co-determination and co-administration by workers in workplaces and in the whole economy.

school-vouchers.rationale: Section IV.6 demands a wholly public, free and secular school system and no state funds for religious schooling.

national-self-determination.rationale: Section VI states the right of self-determination of all peoples, claims it for the party's own people, and Bauer's Brunn programme recognises each nationality's right to national existence.

class-collaboration.rationale: Section III says cooperation between hostile classes can only be a passing phase because class antagonism breaks it up.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Sections II and V aim to make the cultural heritage the property of the whole people and to preserve research and art through the community.

workers-nation.rationale: Section VI subordinates sectional interests of each country's workers to the interest of the international working class.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Section IV.4 demands repeal of all laws that disadvantage women and equal access to public service and professions.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Section II.4 says the working class fights every oppression, whether directed against a class, a sex, a nation or a race.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Sections II.4 and VI call for equality in rights of sexes, peoples and worldviews and fight oppression of any group.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Section III.4 describes the state as an instrument of class rule that the working class must turn into the commonwealth of a classless people.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The programme assigns the state wide economic, social, educational and cultural tasks.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Section V says socialist order cannot be built in a single small country dependent on capitalist powers, and socialisation proceeds only as far as other states have matured.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Section IV.7 demands one marriage law for all citizens without regard to confession and civil registration by the state.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Section IV.7 gives each person the free decision on belonging to any religious or non-religious community.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Section IV.7 makes all education secular, leaving religious instruction to the communities outside general lessons and at their own cost.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The programme bases government on the controlled majority of the people, with the majority's continuing control through democratic guarantees.

population-transfer.rationale: Section VI fights every disenfranchisement of national minorities and Bauer's programme protects minorities through autonomous public corporations.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The programme itself provides expropriation of large property and dictatorship against resisting classes, which contradicts the absolute principle.

vanguard-party.rationale: Section II.2 aims to unite and educate the whole working class in one mass party, and the school distanced itself from Bolshevism.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The programme defends the right of association and, even for socialised firms, says it would not limit the right to strike.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Section I traces the distress of workers and small producers to capitalist production and finance, not to population.

party-controls-media.rationale: Section IV demands freedom of press and section V says means of intellectual production (press, publishing, theatre) must not be monopolised.

party-commands-army.rationale: The programme wants a republican army belonging to the state, loyal to the republic whatever majority governs.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Section VI aims at an international federation of national socialist commonwealths and an international legal order above national disputes.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Section VI wants the League of Nations democratised and turned into a real guardian of peace and an international legal order protecting weak peoples.

clerical-rule.rationale: The programme treats religion as a private matter, removes churches from state power and rejects clerical influence on politics.

abortion-legal.rationale: Section IV.5 demands that abortion by a doctor in a public hospital be exempt from punishment on the woman's request, under health, social or economic grounds, rather than combated by penalties.

free-public-college.rationale: Section IV.6 demands tuition and teaching materials free at all levels, including universities, plus stipends.

arms-reduction.rationale: Section VI demands planned international disarmament within an international legal order.

workers-own-party.rationale: The whole programme is the platform of a workers' party that unites the working class independently of bourgeois parties.

workers-parties-campaign-reforms.rationale: Section IV lists immediate reforms within capitalist society while the party keeps the socialist end as the aim.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Section IV.4 demands repeal of all laws that disadvantage women legally, which covers property and inheritance law.

women-suffrage.rationale: Section IV.4 demands equal rights of women in public service and removal of all legal disadvantages.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Section IV.7 makes all worldviews and religions equal before the law and denies the state a role in church governance.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The Brunn programme Bauer defends gives each nation autonomous self-government and minorities within a territory the status of autonomous public corporations running their own schools.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The Brunn programme replaces historic crown lands with nationally delimited self-governing bodies with their own legislatures.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The Brunn programme joins all self-governing areas of one nation into a single national association, though as a union of bodies rather than one territory.

single-official-language.rationale: The Brunn programme says the party recognises no national privilege and so rejects the demand for a state language, leaving only a mediating language to parliament.

minority-language-support.rationale: The programme gives minorities autonomous schools and legal aid before offices and courts in their language.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Bauer defines the nation as community of character produced by shared fate, transmitted through common language and culture, not by state or religion; he does not name language alone.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Bauer argues that Jews in western Europe have no special question beyond the class struggle and in the east proletarians must fight antisemitism and nationalism together with their neighbours.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Bauer explains the origin of each nation by labour methods, tools and productive forces, and the programme says capitalism itself creates the conditions of its overcoming.

ban-cartels.rationale: The programme demands a cartel law and state oversight of cartels, yet treats concentration as the condition that makes socialisation possible.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Section IV demands the dismantling of tariffs and freer division of labour between peoples.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Section V states that capitalism itself creates the preconditions for socialism and that the mass of the people must seize the means of production.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The programme demands abolition of entailed estates and private hunting rights, and Bauer praises the end of estate privileges.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Section I.6 condemns imperialist subjugation of other cultures and section VI supports the liberation struggles of all peoples.

elective-rulers.rationale: The programme founds the republic on elected representation and celebrates the overthrow of dynastic rule.

minority-veto.rationale: The programme's whole strategy is conquest of power by the majority of the people through universal suffrage.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The programme puts legislation in the hands of elected representative bodies, and Bauer praises binding state power to laws passed by parliaments.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Section III wants the mass of the people to take the most active part in building socialism.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Section III says in the democratic republic bourgeois rule rests on economic power, tradition, press, school and church keeping the majority under its spiritual influence.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Section III names the press, the school and the church as instruments by which the bourgeoisie holds the majority.

corporate-influence.rationale: Section I.4 says industrial concerns force their will on governments and parliaments and the big banks exert the strongest influence on state and society.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Section I.4 describes the working people falling under the oppressive rule of a small number of capital magnates and calls the economic dictatorship of finance capital intolerable.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Section IV demands higher taxes on property income than on earned income and section V abolishes exploitative property.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Section V abolishes exploitative property of capitalists and large landowners but not the working property of small artisans and farmers.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Section V says the development of capitalism itself concentrates production and creates the conditions for socialising it.

alienated-labor.rationale: Section I.2 says the wage worker's lifelong labour in another's service, in a division of labour whose plan he cannot influence, robs it of meaning and aim.

social-market-economy.rationale: The programme aims to overcome capitalism, not to combine it with social protection, though it pursues the reforms meanwhile.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Section IV demands keeping an army strong enough to put down any counter-revolutionary rising.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The programme overthrows dynastic rule and founds office on election.

property-franchise.rationale: The party celebrates breaking the franchise privileges of the propertied classes through universal suffrage.

racial-franchise.rationale: The programme is built on universal suffrage and opposes oppression on grounds of race.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Section IV.7 declares the legal impediments to marriage of differing religion invalid before the state.

civil-marriage.rationale: Section IV.7 demands marriage before state authorities, with a church wedding optional afterwards.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Section IV.7 demands a uniform state marriage law and state registers.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Section IV.7 says social democracy does not fight religion and treats it as a private matter.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The programme demands republican police and gendarmerie and a social-pedagogical reform of prisons, not abolition.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The programme demands expanded public insurance and municipal social care instead of charity.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Demanding repeal of every law disadvantaging women covers marital law that places authority with the husband.

rent-control.rationale: Section IV defends and wants to expand tenant protection and public housing.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Section VI resists any imperialist or nationalist war and pledges not to be dragged into war, while keeping an army for the republic's defence.

communal-electorates.rationale: Religion is to be a private matter and no community of belief is to be a political body.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Section III aims to adapt the existing state apparatus to the needs of the working class and use it to socialise capital, not to destroy it.

indirect-election.rationale: The programme calls for election of judges directly by the people or by their representative bodies, so it names both direct and indirect routes.

national-church-status.rationale: Section IV.7 makes all churches private-law bodies without privilege.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The programme demands guaranteed personal freedom and trial by independent courts and Bauer cites the right to trial as a liberal gain to defend.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Section IV demands abolition of consumption taxes on necessities of mass consumption.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Section IV extends compulsory insurance to all wage earners, small traders, small farmers and professionals rather than targeting the poorest.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The programme is an organised party's plan to win power through elections and parliamentary government.

remove-indigenous-peoples.rationale: Section I.6 condemns the imperialist subjection of peoples of other cultures by violence and section VI supports their liberation.

no-central-bank.rationale: Section IV demands strict state oversight of the note bank, not its abolition.

religious-offensive-war.rationale: Section VI opposes every imperialist and nationalist war with all its strength.

divinely-chosen-superior-people.rationale: Section VI demands equality of peoples and Bauer's programme recognises each nation's equal right.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The programme derives authority from the majority of the people and treats religion as private.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The programme's overthrow of the dynasty and its secular state exclude a sacred ruler.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Section IV demands progressive taxes and a tax-free minimum.

abolish-income-tax.rationale: Section IV builds its tax policy on progressive income taxation.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Sections III and V say class rule and class struggle are overcome as expropriation ends the split into exploiting and exploited classes.

land-redistribution.rationale: Section V puts large estates under community ownership, to be leased in part to small farmers, tenants and farm labourers as the Agrarian Programme decides.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: Section V keeps the work property of farmers and small tradespeople.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Section I.6 condemns colonial conquest of backward territories as markets and raw material sources.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The programme promises democratic guarantees and freedom of press, association and assembly.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Section IV.7 treats all worldviews as equal before the law and the state as not enforcing religious rules.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The programme's secular state and democratic rule exclude religious tests of legitimacy.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Section IV.7 gives everyone the free choice of religious community and denies the state any compulsion in religion.

more-religion-public.rationale: Section IV.7 makes schools and state secular and removes religion from public funding.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The programme turns churches into private-law bodies without public funds, expropriates church landed estates and removes theological faculties from universities.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Section IV.7 makes all schooling secular and says worldviews should be reconciled with the results of science.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Bauer rejects racial substance as the basis of nations but states no position on average ability differences.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The sources record no position on this.

open-borders.rationale: Section IV demands the international abolition of restrictions on freedom of movement along with tariffs, so that labour can move.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The same demand for abolishing restrictions on freedom of movement runs against cutting immigration.

race-based-immigration-restrictions.rationale: The programme opposes oppression on grounds of race and demands abolition of freedom-of-movement restrictions.

free-trade.rationale: Section IV wants protective tariffs dismantled so that the division of labour between peoples can raise productivity and living standards.

limit-growth.rationale: Section IV makes raising labour productivity the condition of rising living standards.

nation-first.rationale: Section VI subordinates the sectional interests of workers in each country to the international working class and demands peaceful relations with all states.

rehabilitation.rationale: Section IV demands social-pedagogical prison regime and criminal law reform on social and democratic principles.

strong-leader.rationale: Section II.4 sets the people's demand for freedom and self-determination against the rule of authority.

state-harmful.rationale: The programme uses the state as the main instrument of socialisation and sees the future commonwealth as the state's successor form.

natural-rulers.rationale: The programme frames the class struggle as authority against self-determination and ends in self-government of the people, though it also demands advancement of the able.

decide-locally.rationale: The 1926 programme wants a unitary republic with expanded municipal autonomy, while Bauer's earlier Brunn programme proposed a federal state of national bodies.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Bauer values the development of each nation's culture, yet the programme's class ideal is to overthrow the spell of tradition.

change-traditions-that-no-longer-suit.rationale: Section II.4 describes the labour side as striving for transformation against the spell of tradition.

parliamentary-road-socialism.rationale: Section III says the working class can win state power by the decision of universal suffrage and exercise it democratically, provided the army and republic are defended.

socialism-needs-revolutionary-war.rationale: The programme's normal path is democratic conquest of power; only a counter-revolution could force civil war.

no-transition-to-communism.rationale: Section V describes a transition period in which socialised and capitalist firms exist side by side.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: Section VI fights every disenfranchisement of national minorities.

country-wealth-only-from-land.rationale: The programme treats wealth as the product of workers' labour in industry, trade and transport as well as farming.

unions-run-economy.rationale: Section V puts socialised firms under the community, warning against sectional interests of one group of workers.

worker-farmer-alliance.rationale: Section II.3 calls small peasants, with the petty bourgeoisie, allies of the working class, though large farmers belong to the bourgeoisie.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Bauer treats antisemitism as a naive form of anti-capitalism to be replaced by the class struggle, rejecting the idea of a Jewish conspiracy.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Bauer tells socialists to fight capital because it is capital, not because it is Jewish.

unpaid-domestic-work-exploitation.rationale: The sources record no position on this.

municipal-businesses-mixed-economy.rationale: Section IV promotes state and municipal enterprises and cooperatives alongside capitalist firms in the present order.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Section IV wants municipal housing, medicine supply and social care run by communes and public bodies.

municipal-property.rationale: Section V lets the national state, provinces or municipalities own socialised firms, so ownership is not confined to localities.

labour-priority-over-capital.rationale: Section V aims to abolish the command of capital over production and to put labour first through socialisation.

constitutional-jury-trial.rationale: Section IV demands jurors and lay judges decide in all criminal cases, though it does not say this should be entrenched.

political-decisions-consensus.rationale: The programme's method is majority rule through elections.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Section III looks to the most active participation of the mass of the people, and section IV to co-determination and municipal self-government.

free-basic-services-for-all.rationale: Section IV demands free tuition and teaching materials, free medicines through the communes and free public medical services for schools.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: Section VI supports the liberation struggles of all peoples against imperialist foreign rule.

arbitrator-settles-disputes.rationale: Section VI aims at an international legal order able to settle all disputes between peoples peacefully.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Bauer lists binding state power to laws made by national representatives, applied by independent judges, as a liberal gain that fascism destroyed.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Sections III and V make the working class's conquest of state power the way to the socialised order.

socialized-care.rationale: Section IV demands public day homes and housing facilities to ease housework while also valuing women's role as mothers.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Section V says capital ownership loses its function when the owner becomes a mere shareholder, which makes its abolition possible.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The sources record no position on this statement, and no stated principle of the programme settles it.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The sources record no position on this statement, and no stated principle of the programme settles it.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The sources record no position on this statement, and no stated principle of the programme settles it.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The sources record no position on this statement, and no stated principle of the programme settles it.

limit-guns.rationale: The sources record no position on this statement, and no stated principle of the programme settles it.

empower-police-military.rationale: The sources record no position on this statement, and no stated principle of the programme settles it.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The sources record no position on this statement, and no stated principle of the programme settles it.

traditional-family.rationale: The sources record no position on this statement, and no stated principle of the programme settles it.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The sources record no position on this statement, and no stated principle of the programme settles it.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The sources record no position on this statement, and no stated principle of the programme settles it.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The sources record no position on this statement, and no stated principle of the programme settles it.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The sources record no position on this statement, and no stated principle of the programme settles it.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The sources record no position on this statement, and no stated principle of the programme settles it.

notes: Answers rest on the Linz Programme (1926), Bauer's 1907 book and Brunn programme, and his articles; none of Adler's, Hilferding's or Renner's own works was read, so positions held only by them are null. Themes searched without a position: environment, technology, criminal justice detail, culture-war questions, identity politics, trade-bloc and nuclear issues, constitutional design beyond a unitary republic, electoral systems. The Linz Programme's unitary republic and Bauer's earlier national federal programme differ, so local-power answers are mixed or null. The 1926 Anschluss goal is a peaceful union of states by self-determination and is not read as a claim on foreign territory.
